TROUBLESHOOTING · QUICK FIXES

Azeroth Survivors troubleshooting: lag, crashes, and saves

Start with the error message you see. These steps separate browser support, graphics, performance, server load, and save problems.

FIND YOUR FIX

Lag and stutterToo many playersCrashes and freezingSlow downloadNo WebGPUNo usable GPUBlack screen or loadingMissing saveDownload safety

PERFORMANCE

Fix Azeroth Survivors lag, stutter, and low FPS

  • Lower the game's Render Scale in Options; this is often the most direct graphics workload reduction.
  • Plug in a laptop and confirm the browser is using its high-performance GPU.
  • Close heavy tabs and background applications before late waves, when many enemies can be visible together.
  • On mobile, a brief stutter while shaders compile may settle. If the tab crashes, reopen the game and reduce graphics settings if available.

Slow first-time loading and low frame rate are different problems: loading is about data and connection; FPS is about graphics workload and hardware.

If the game is lagging when enemies pile up, lower Render Scale and close heavy tabs or background applications. If the whole run feels laggy from the first wave, check those same local settings. If it lags only when many people share the room, check the server-load section next.

SERVER LOAD

“Too many people are playing”

This message means the game host is busy or enforcing a request limit. Wait a little and try again. If the browser host remains unavailable, the creator's official page may link a Windows build. Avoid downloads from third-party mirrors.

BROWSER CRASHES

Azeroth Survivors keeps crashing or freezing

If the browser crashes during loading, check whether it reports no WebGPU or no usable GPU. The adapter steps cover hardware acceleration, browser restart, GPU status, and remote desktop limitations. If the browser still cannot use a graphics adapter, update the graphics driver as described in the adapter steps.

If the game freezes partway through a run, close heavy tabs and background applications, then lower Render Scale in Options. On a Windows laptop with two graphics processors, set the browser to High performance and restart it. Try these local graphics steps before assuming that a stalled frame is the server-load message. The first run walkthrough shows the normal opening sequence, and the zone order and unlocks guide covers later runs.

If the tab is black when you return to it, follow the black-screen steps. A private window or strict storage setting can interfere with cached data.

DOWNLOAD SPEED

Azeroth Survivors slow download

If the game is downloading slow on a first visit, distinguish the transfer from a page that remains on its loading screen. For a long loading screen or a black page, use the loading steps. Give the first load time to finish; if the loading screen does not advance, reload once and check whether it starts again.

Try a supported browser if the transfer or first load continues to stall. Close tabs and background programs using the connection, and avoid other downloads at the same time. If another download is running, pause it before retrying the game transfer. If the game already opened but runs slowly, the lag section above addresses graphics workload; Render Scale does not change how long the initial download takes.

The creator's official page may provide a Windows build as an alternative to the browser version. For questions about where to obtain it, see download safety.

BROWSER SUPPORT

“This browser has no WebGPU”

  1. Update to a current Chrome or Edge. A supported recent Safari may also work depending on your device and OS.
  2. Restart the browser after updating and reopen the creator's game page.
  3. On Linux Chrome, WebGPU may require enabling chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu, then relaunching.
  4. If you are using Firefox or an older device, try a supported browser or the official Windows build linked from the creator's page.

The game relies on WebGPU for its browser renderer. This error usually means a browser or operating-system capability is missing, not that the save is broken.

GRAPHICS ADAPTER

WebGPU is present, but no usable GPU

  • Turn on hardware acceleration in Chrome or Edge settings, then fully restart the browser.
  • On Windows laptops with two graphics processors, open Settings → System → Display → Graphics, set the browser to High performance, then restart it.
  • Update the graphics driver. In Chrome, chrome://gpu can show why acceleration or WebGPU is disabled.
  • Try outside a remote desktop session if possible; remote sessions may not expose a supported graphics adapter.

If the browser says WebGPU exists but it still cannot start, the issue is often the selected GPU or driver rather than the browser version.

FIRST LOAD

Black screen or a long loading screen

On a first visit, the browser has to fetch game data and compile graphics shaders. Keep the tab open and wait for the game's own loading screen before deciding the page is stuck.

  1. Reload once after checking your connection and browser support.
  2. Close the page and reopen the official game URL if the loading screen never advances.
  3. Check that browser storage is available; private browsing or strict storage settings can interfere with cached data.
  4. If it remains black, check the browser's GPU status and try the graphics steps above.

A black screen can also come from a graphics driver crash, especially on a device that barely meets the graphics requirements.

PROGRESS RECOVERY

My save disappeared or did not transfer

The game stores browser progress with the browser site data. These steps can make it look like a save vanished:

  • You opened a private window, another browser, or a different device.
  • You cleared site data or cookies for the game host.
  • You played from a different website. Browsers keep saves for different website addresses separate, even when both pages open the same game.

Go back to the exact game page where you played. Before clearing browser data or changing devices, use the game's Options → Saves → Export Save. At the destination, use Import Save. Importing replaces the destination save, so export that save first if you need to preserve it.

This guide does not host the game. Play through the creator's website so the game's own save and update behavior stays under the developer's control.

Read the full save transfer and backup guide.

DOWNLOAD SAFETY

Is the download safe?

Use the browser game at the creator's site, or follow the Windows download linked from that same page. Avoid copies that ask for a Battle.net password, payment, an unrelated launcher, or a download hosted by an unknown file-sharing site.

A free fan build may not have a recognized publisher signature. That alone does not prove a file is unsafe; only download from the developer's own page and scan unfamiliar files before running them.
